caption:
Cleveland-Cliffs, ArcBest and Valero: shareholder returns next to an EPA civil penalty

From the archive: 2020 to 2023.

ArcBest, Mar 20, 2023
The math: $91.5 million (ArcBest share repurchases, 2023) ÷ $535,000 (civil penalty the EPA announced for subsidiary ABF Freight, Mar 2023; ABF does not admit liability) = about 171 times the civil penalty

Cleveland-Cliffs, Feb 14, 2022
The math: $240 million (returned through share repurchases, 2022) ÷ $3 million (civil penalty the EPA announced Feb 2022; the decree says no admission of liability) = 80 times the civil penalty

Valero Energy, Oct 19, 2020
The math: $1.8 billion (returned to stockholders, mostly dividends, 2020) ÷ $2,850,000 (civil penalty the EPA announced Oct 2020; Valero does not admit liability) = about 631 times the civil penalty

Three 10-K sentences. Three EPA announcements. Same years. (Our take.)

Sources: ArcBest, Form 10-K, filed Feb 23, 2024; ArcBest: U.S. EPA, enforcement announcement, published Mar 20, 2023; Cleveland-Cliffs, Form 10-K, filed Feb 14, 2023; Cleveland-Cliffs: U.S. EPA, enforcement announcement, published Feb 14, 2022; Valero Energy, Form 10-K, filed Feb 23, 2021; Valero Energy: U.S. EPA, enforcement announcement, published Oct 19, 2020.
